skill.description: Standardising Technical Output Writing (STOW) applies exact output contracts, preserves code, commands, paths, identifiers, quotations, and data values, and reviews editable prose for focus, technical clarity, terminology, evidence strength, and recurrent synthetic-writing pathologies. Use when the user explicitly invokes STOW or asks to write, rewrite, review, or validate a README, runbook, procedure, plan, audit, handoff, public technical document, controlled-technical text, mixed prose with protected literals, or an exact JSON, JSONL, YAML, or Markdown artefact.
skill.summary: A contract-first writing assistant for precise technical prose, protected literals, and validated structured artifacts.
skill.author: theislampill

content.value_statement: Technical documents often lose precision when prose, commands, paths, and structured data are edited inconsistently. STOW applies output contracts and focused prose review while preserving protected literals.
actual_capabilities: Applies precedence rules to technical prose, procedures, plans, audits, handoffs, and structured artifacts.
Preserves code, commands, paths, identifiers, quotations, and data values in protected regions.
Reviews prose for clarity, terminology consistency, evidence strength, repetition, and synthetic writing patterns.
Validates JSON, JSONL, YAML, Markdown artifacts, and supported coordination schemas through packaged helpers.
Looks up individual STOW rules and resolves applicable profiles and documented rule conflicts.
limitations: It does not execute user commands or guarantee that a generated procedure works in a target environment.
Advisory prose checks do not replace human semantic review or domain expertise.
Protected-region masking may miss unusual formatting outside its supported syntax.
Structured validation requires the documented Python dependencies for the applicable helper.

use_cases.title: Polish technical documentation
use_cases.description: Rewrite a README or public technical document for direct structure, precise claims, consistent terminology, and preserved command examples.

use_cases.title: Prepare operational procedures
use_cases.description: Shape runbooks, plans, audits, and handoffs into bounded steps with visible evidence, limitations, verification, and rollback details.

use_cases.title: Validate structured deliverables
use_cases.description: Check JSON, JSONL, YAML, or Markdown artifacts against their contracts while retaining literal values and reporting structural defects.

prompt_templates.title: Clean up a README
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this README for direct technical clarity. Preserve every command, path, identifier, quotation, and data value. Return only the revised README.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: improve a short public document without changing its technical literals.

prompt_templates.title: Review a runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this runbook for missing preconditions, unclear actions, unsupported claims, and absent verification or rollback details. List concrete corrections and preserve all commands exactly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: audit an operational procedure before team use.

prompt_templates.title: Check a structured artifact
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this JSON, JSONL, YAML, or Markdown artifact against the stated contract. Report parse and structural issues, distinguish warnings from failures, and do not rewrite protected values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess a contract-bound artifact with mixed prose and structured data.

prompt_templates.title: Audit rule applicability
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply STOW to this technical document. Classify each region, identify the active profile and relevant rule conflicts, preserve protected literals, and return the smallest complete set of corrections with evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: perform a focused, evidence-based rule audit across mixed content.

output_examples.input: Rewrite a deployment README while preserving its commands and configuration names.
output_examples.output: A concise README with the installation path first, direct headings, consistent terminology, and unchanged commands and configuration names.

output_examples.input: Review a migration runbook for operational completeness.
output: Add a precondition stating the required backup and access checks.
Add a verification result and rollback action to the migration step.
Keep the existing service name, command text, and evidence references unchanged.

output_examples.input: Check a handoff artifact against its schema and report the result.
output_examples.output: The report separates parse failures, schema violations, unresolved references, and advisory prose concerns so the owner can correct the artifact.

best_practices: State the output contract and protected literals before requesting a rewrite.
Provide authoritative sources for claims, numbers, terminology, and required formats.
Use the named validator on the actual final artifact when the format has a supported schema.
anti_patterns: Do not ask STOW to invent commands, evidence, versions, citations, or current system state.
Do not treat advisory prose findings as proof of a security, correctness, or authorship defect.
Do not label editable text as protected when the requested change requires literal editing.

faq.question: What is STOW?
faq.answer: STOW is a contract-first assistant for precise technical writing and validated structured artifacts.

faq.question: Which tools support STOW?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible hosts.

faq.question: What content can STOW review?
faq.answer: It reviews READMEs, runbooks, procedures, plans, audits, handoffs, mixed prose, and JSON, JSONL, YAML, or Markdown artifacts.

faq.question: Does STOW change commands or paths?
faq.answer: It preserves protected commands, paths, identifiers, quotations, and data values unless literal editing is explicitly requested.

faq.question: Are prose lint results blocking?
faq.answer: The packaged prose linter is report-only. Its advisories support review and do not replace human judgment.

faq.question: Can STOW validate schemas?
faq.answer: Yes. Its packaged validator checks supported structured formats and named coordination schemas when the required dependencies are installed.
